editorial: Despite being a developing economy, Bolivia is not inexpensive. This is not uncommon for countries that depend on tourism to subsidise the rest of the economy.
We spent $1000 over the course of 5 days, including $215 on visas.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: With more money, we’d spend more time in Bolivia by taking the three-day tour that included Laguna Colorada.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: We kept things pretty tight, so there’s not a lot of room to cut corners!

categories.title: STAYS
editorial: Our nights in Sucre and Santa Cruz were inexpensive at about $15 a night. But Uyuni was $200 for three nights at the Cagnapa hotel.
It’s important to pick a place with heating in Uyuni, which pushes up the prices.

categories.title: FOOD & DRINKS
editorial: Similar to the stays, food was inexpensive in Sucre and Santa Cruz, but steeply priced in Uyuni. A meal for two at the popular Tika in Uyuni cost about $25.
Service in Uyuni is painfully slow, so don’t wait till you’re hangry to grab a bite.

categories.title: EXPERIENCES
editorial: The day-long tour of the salt flats was $60 per person. Our guide took incredible photos and videos, so a $30 tip felt fair (we would have been more generous if we weren’t running out of cash).

categories.title: INTER-CITY TRAVEL
editorial: The round trip between Santa Cruz and Sucre cost us $70 each. And buses to and fro Uyuni was $26 each.

categories.title: MISCELLANEOUS
editorial: At least in 2023, Bolivia had a hefty visa fee of around $110 per person!
Luckily, Ubers were super cheap and only cost us $10 in total to get from the airports to our destinations.

title: What it's Going to Cost
